regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"India GDP at 7.8% YoY looks like acceleration — until you note that IIP overall slipped to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%, and core sector decelerated to 5.4% YoY from 6.0%. The PMI composite at 54.6 is services-led (54.5) while manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8; goods-economy proxies are softening even as the headline flatters. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is the one number that earns optimism — it's above the threshold that historically triggers private capex — but the IIP deceleration suggests that trigger hasn't fully fired yet.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"The CPI headline at 4.45% YoY is almost reassuring — until fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising two months straight) reminds you that the RBI's own forecast just jumped to 5.1% YoY from 4.6%. Core CPI at 3.9% YoY is benign, which is the only reason the RBI can hold; but WPI at 9.92% YoY means producer margins are being squeezed from both ends — input costs rising, demand not yet strong enough to pass through fully. Invert the benign core narrative: if Brent sustains above $100/bbl, fuel feeds into transport costs, which feeds into food logistics, and core stops being benign within two quarters.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1% YoY; CD ratio 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% YoY is a 630bps divergence that the CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (75th percentile historically) only partially captures. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held — FY14 — the system needed emergency macro-prudential intervention within 18 months. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY from 10.6% signals wholesale funding is being tapped to bridge the gap; industry credit at 20% YoY and services at 22.9% YoY are both running well ahead of what deposit mobilisation can support. The regulator is watching — risk-weight tightening on specific segments is the most likely first move.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. with CPI at 4.45% YoY gives a real rate of roughly 80bps — positive, but thin. The RBI's own inflation forecast revision to 5.1% YoY effectively narrows that buffer to near zero on a forward basis, making a cut this cycle increasingly implausible without a sharp commodity reversal. For housing, the average home loan rate at 7.75% p.a. is already compressing affordability; for corporate capex, the real borrowing cost is rising even without a repo move, because term spreads are widening. The RBI is not cutting — and the market pricing any easing in the next two quarters is mispriced.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%, now at 74th percentile) is the most unambiguously positive signal in today's data. The 77% threshold matters: historically, private capex announcements accelerate meaningfully above 76-77% utilisation as the IRR on new capacity turns positive. The inversion: core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0%) and IIP overall at 6.7% YoY (down from 8.8%) suggest the capex signal is real but the goods-production follow-through is lagging. Watch cement dispatch and steel consumption in the next print — those are the ground-truth proxies for whether announced capex is becoming physical investment.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹199853 cr/mo; PV 16% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹199,853 cr / month (14.8% YoY growth) is the strongest consumption signal in the data — but the question is always: how much of this is genuine demand versus formalisation reclassifying existing spend? Passenger vehicle sales at 16% YoY and two-wheeler at 19.7% YoY suggest the answer is 'mostly real demand' this cycle, with two-wheelers confirming rural and mass-market participation. The tension: credit card growth at just 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) suggests urban discretionary consumers are either tapping out or switching to UPI/debit — a deceleration in the highest-margin consumption segment that the GST headline obscures.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 10.8% YoY creates a 350 bps divergence. CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits (down from 82.5% prior month) but still at 75th percentile historically. Credit-to-deposit gap has widened for 3 consecutive months. NBFC credit growth accelerating at 14.9% YoY (up from 10.6% YoY prior), signalling wholesale funding pressure. Industry credit at 20% YoY and services credit at 22.9% YoY — both outpacing deposit mobilisation.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% — they'll poach deposits from smaller lenders. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; they face margin compression and refinancing risk. Watch for RBI to signal rate cuts in Q2 to ease deposit pressure. Corporate bond issuance at ₹18,700 cr / month (at 0th percentile, a structural low) suggests corporates are rationing credit — a leading indicator of credit stress ahead.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile is elevated but not extreme. Historically, ratios above 85% preceded NBFC funding crises (2018–19). Current divergence is manageable if deposit growth re-accelerates; if it stalls, RBI will be forced to cut rates despite inflation overshoot.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY (latest), capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6% prior month, at 74th percentile). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6% prior) but still positive. Nifty 50 at 22,776 index (73rd percentile), Bank Nifty at 55,128 index (91st percentile). GST collections at ₹199,853 cr / month (71st percentile), up 14.8% YoY from ₹174,116 cr / month. Vehicle credit at 18.8% YoY and agricultural credit at 17% YoY (both up sharply from prior periods).","implication":"Overweight capital goods, cement, and steel stocks — capacity utilisation at 77.4% leaves room for 3–5 years of capex-led growth before bottlenecks emerge. Favour PSU banks and NBFCs financing infrastructure; credit demand will remain robust. Avoid consumer discretionary plays; GST strength is broad-based but not concentrated in durables. Position for a 12–18 month capex cycle; watch for capacity utilisation to breach 80% as a signal to rotate into defensive sectors.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is mid-cycle, historically preceding 18–24 months of sustained capex. The last time CU was this level (2021–22), capex growth sustained at 15%+ for 6 quarters. Current IIP capgoods at 16.1% is above the 10-year median, confirming the cycle is real.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit Record; Affluent Money Entering","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (latest, 92nd percentile), up from ₹31,961 cr / month prior month — rising 2 in a row. SIP YoY growth at 14% (down from 16% prior, at 36th percentile). SIP accounts at 100.18 mn (82nd percentile), up from 99.06 mn. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr (93rd percentile), up from ₹18.21 lakh cr — rising 2 in a row. MF AUM at ₹87.08 lakh cr (86th percentile), up from ₹85.76 lakh cr. DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, at all-time high), up from ₹35,099 cr net / month. FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile), up from ₹20,200 cr net / month.","implication":"SIP inflows are at record absolute levels (₹32,297 cr / month) but YoY growth is decelerating (14% vs 16% prior). This signals a shift: SIP AUM growing 40%+ while account growth is 10%+ means average ticket size is rising sharply — affluent money is entering, not mass retail. This is late-cycle behaviour. Maintain overweight on large-cap, quality names; avoid micro-cap and speculative plays. DII at all-time high (₹58,502 cr net / month) suggests domestic institutions are front-running a potential market correction — a contrarian signal to trim longs.","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile are near all-time highs. Historically, when SIP inflows peak and YoY growth decelerates simultaneously, it precedes a 6–12 month consolidation. The 2021 peak saw similar dynamics before the 2022 correction.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI's Credibility","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest, 95th percentile), up from 20.05% YoY prior month — rising 2 in a row. WPI at 9.92% YoY (67th percentile), up from 9.78% YoY. CPI headline at 4.45% YoY (41st percentile), up from 4.38% YoY. CPI core at 3.9% YoY (28th percentile, at low end). RBI inflation forecast at 5.1% YoY (53rd percentile), up from 4.6% YoY. Brent crude at $101.08 / bbl (71st percentile), flat from prior. FAO food index at 130.3 index (57th percentile), up from 129.7 index.","implication":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY is a structural problem, not cyclical. This will keep headline CPI sticky above 4.5% for the next 2–3 quarters, constraining RBI's ability to cut rates despite slowing growth. Overweight energy stocks and refiners (they benefit from high fuel prices and weak rupee). Underweight consumer staples and discretionary — margin compression is inevitable. Watch for RBI to hold rates at 5.25% p.a. through Q2 2026, creating a growth-inflation trap. This is a headwind for equity valuations; expect 10–15% multiple compression if rates stay elevated.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in the dataset's history. The last time fuel inflation exceeded 20% YoY (2021–22), it persisted for 8+ quarters and forced RBI to hike rates despite growth concerns. Current trajectory suggests similar persistence.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Cycle Resumes; Carry Unwind Risk","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.75% p.a. (latest, 68th percentile), up from 3.63% p.a. prior — rising 2 in a row. US 10Y Treasury yield at 5.31% yield (96th percentile), up from 5.28% yield — rising 4 of last 5 months. US core CPI at 2.4462% YoY (47th percentile), down from 2.4665% YoY. US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR (50th percentile), up from 2.5% SAAR. BOJ rate at 1% p.a. (86th percentile), up from 0.75% p.a. — a 25 bps hike. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% p.a. (59th percentile), up from 2% p.a. DXY at 101.939 index (55th percentile), flat. US PMI composite at 56 index (84th percentile), up from 54.5 index.","implication":"Fed is re-tightening (funds rate up 12 bps in 2 months) while BOJ is hiking (1% p.a., a structural shift). This is a carry unwind scenario: JPY will strengthen, USD will weaken, and EM carry trades (INR, BRL, MXN) face pressure. Reduce long positions in INR carry trades. Overweight USD-denominated assets and short JPY crosses. US 10Y at 5.31% yield (96th percentile) is a structural headwind for global equities — expect 15–20% multiple compression in high-beta EM stocks. India's FII flows will reverse if US yields stay elevated; watch for outflows in Q2 2026.","pct_10y":96,"pct_note":"US 10Y at 96th percentile is near all-time highs. Historically, when US 10Y exceeds 5.25% yield, EM equity flows reverse within 4–8 weeks. The 2022 taper tantrum saw similar dynamics.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"Rupee Weakening Despite Strong Domestic Flows","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 ₹ (latest, 91st percentile), down from 96.36 ₹ prior month — but up 3 of last 5 months (weakening trend). FII equity net at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile), up from ₹20,200 cr net / month. DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile). India VIX at 13.608 index (9th percentile, very low), down from 14.78 index. US VIX at 15.01 index (9th percentile), flat. Brent crude at $101.08 / bbl (71st percentile). Gold in INR at ₹12,942 / g (100th percentile), up from ₹12,878 / g.","implication":"Rupee is weakening (96.15 ₹ per USD, at 91st percentile) despite strong domestic equity inflows (DII at all-time high). This suggests RBI is intervening to prevent sharper depreciation — a sign of reserve depletion risk. The rupee weakness is driven by: (1) Fed re-tightening (US 10Y at 96th percentile), (2) oil prices elevated at $101.08 / bbl, and (3) India's current account deficit widening. Reduce long INR positions; hedge with USD forwards. Watch for RBI to signal reserve adequacy concerns in Q2 2026 if rupee breaches 97 ₹ per USD. Gold at ₹12,942 / g (100th percentile) is a safe haven bid — expect further INR weakness if global risk-off accelerates.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile is near all-time weakness. Historically, when INR weakens to this level despite strong domestic flows, it signals RBI is managing a structural CAD problem, not a cyclical one. The 2013 taper tantrum saw similar dynamics.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Shift, Not IT Crisis","data_text":"Office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (latest, 6th percentile, at structural low), down from 13.7 mn sq ft / quarter prior. Office vacancy at 14.5% vacant (42nd percentile), down from 15.3% vacant. Rent in Bengaluru at ₹163 / sqft / mo (95th percentile), up from ₹148 / sqft / mo — rising 2 of last 5 quarters. Rent in Mumbai at ₹335 / sqft / mo (100th percentile), up from ₹322 / sqft / mo — rising 2 of last 5 quarters. Retail mall vacancy at 4.8% vacant (7th percentile, at structural low), down from 5% vacant. Nifty 50 at 22,776 index (73rd percentile), flat. Bank Nifty at 55,128 index (91st percentile). IT credit growth at 20% YoY (78th percentile), up from 6.5% YoY prior.","implication":"Office absorption is collapsing (13.2 mn sq ft / quarter, 6th percentile) while rents in Bengaluru and Mumbai are at all-time highs (95th and 100th percentiles). This is NOT an IT services crisis — it's a structural shift from traditional IT services to Global Capability Centers (GCCs). GCCs are smaller, more efficient, and located in premium micro-markets (Bengaluru, Mumbai). Traditional IT services firms are shedding office space (hence low absorption), but GCCs are consolidating in high-rent zones (hence rent spikes). IT credit growth at 20% YoY confirms GCCs are borrowing to expand, not traditional IT services. Implication: Avoid traditional IT services stocks (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) — they're in structural decline. Overweight commercial real estate plays in Bengaluru and Mumbai (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs) — they'll capture GCC consolidation. This is a 3–5 year structural shift that equity analysts are missing.","pct_10y":6,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 6th percentile is a 10-year low, but rents at 95–100th percentiles is a paradox that resolves only if demand is shifting to premium micro-markets. Historically, this pattern preceded a 2–3 year rotation from traditional office to GCC-focused commercial real estate.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Services Carry the Headline — Goods Economy Quietly Slips

The facts:

  • PMI Composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is services-driven: PMI Services rose to 54.5 while PMI Manufacturing fell to 52.8.
  • IIP overall decelerated to 6.7% YoY from 8.8%; core sector slipped to 5.4% YoY from 6.0% — goods-economy momentum is fading.
  • But capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile, up from 75.6%) crosses the threshold that historically precedes private capex acceleration.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 19.7% YoY and PV sales at 16% YoY confirm mass-market demand is real, not statistical.

The tension: The GDP headline and PMI composite signal expansion; the IIP deceleration and core sector softening signal the goods economy is losing altitude. Services cannot sustain the composite indefinitely if industrial output is rolling over.

Bottom line: Watch IIP capital goods in the next print — a second consecutive deceleration below 12% YoY would signal the capex upcycle is stalling before private investment picks up the baton.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Surveys Accelerate — Bond Market Tightens Anyway

The facts:

  • US PMI Composite rose to 56 (84th percentile) — the strongest survey read in over a year — while US GDP SAAR slipped to 2.2% SAAR from 2.5%.
  • US 10Y Treasury at 5.31% yield (96th percentile, rising 4 of last 5 months) is tightening financial conditions independently of the Fed.
  • BOJ hiked to 1.0% p.a. (86th percentile) from 0.75% — yen carry unwind pressure on EM assets builds with each BOJ move.
  • But China GDP at 4.3% YoY (down from 5.0%) with PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) removes the commodity-reflation backstop for EM exporters.

The tension: DM survey data is pricing re-acceleration; nominal GDP growth is decelerating and real tightening is already embedded in the 10Y yield. The bond market and the PMI are telling opposite stories — one of them is wrong.

Bottom line: Hedge EM duration exposure: US 10Y above 5.3% yield with BOJ normalising is the combination that historically forces EM central banks into defensive holds, regardless of domestic inflation trajectories.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

Domestic Flows at Record Highs — Rupee Weakens Regardless

The facts:

  • DII equity net at ₹58,502 cr net / month (100th percentile, all-time high); SIP inflows at ₹32,297 cr / month (92nd percentile, rising two months straight).
  • FII equity net turned strongly positive at ₹29,631 cr net / month (83rd percentile), up from ₹20,200 cr net / month prior.
  • But INR at 96.15 ₹ (91st percentile, weakening trend — up 3 of last 5 months) is depreciating despite record domestic and recovering foreign equity inflows.
  • Gold in INR at ₹12,942/g (100th percentile) — the rupee hedge is being exercised even as equity flows look robust.

The tension: Record domestic liquidity and recovering FII flows should be INR-supportive; the rupee's persistent weakness points to structural current account pressure from Brent at $101/bbl and the BOJ-driven carry unwind overriding equity flow signals.

Bottom line: SIP AUM at ₹18.62 lakh cr provides a structural equity floor, but INR weakness above 96.5 ₹ would trigger imported inflation feedback — watch that level before adding unhedged domestic duration.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Rents at Records, Absorption at Lows — REITs Caught in Between

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING: NRI share of residential purchases at 20% (up 5 pp vs prior period), with NRI share within premium/luxury at 25% — Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad are the primary destinations.
  • Supply skewed premium: 34% of new launches in the ₹80 lakh–₹1.5 cr band and 24% in luxury ₹1.5–2.5 cr — developers chasing NRI and affluent domestic buyers while affordable supply shrinks.
  • Mumbai office rent at ₹335/sqft/mo (100th percentile) and Bengaluru at ₹163/sqft/mo (95th percentile) — but office absorption at 13.2 mn sq ft / quarter (6th percentile) signals GCC consolidation, not demand expansion.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, and Brookfield at ₹263/unit are all well below prior levels — the rent signal has not translated into REIT unit price recovery.

The tension: Rents at all-time highs and vacancy falling (14.5% vacant, down from 15.3%) should be REIT-positive; absorption at a structural low suggests the rent strength reflects supply discipline, not demand acceleration — a distinction that matters for forward NAV growth.

Bottom line: Overweight residential developers exposed to premium and luxury segments in Hyderabad and Bengaluru where NRI flows are concentrated; avoid office REITs until absorption recovers above 16 mn sq ft / quarter.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Sequencing Matters

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile, rising two months straight) with Brent at $101/bbl — every $10 adds ~$15bn to India's import bill and widens CAD by ~40bps; INR at 96.15 ₹ has no buffer.
  • CD ratio at 81.4% credit ÷ deposits with credit growing at 17.1% YoY vs deposits at 10.8% YoY — NBFC wholesale funding stress is the most likely first fracture point.
  • US 10Y at 5.31% yield (96th percentile) with BOJ at 1.0% p.a. — carry unwind risk for EM flows is the external trigger that could convert domestic stress into a balance-of-payments event.
  • But India VIX at 13.6 (9th percentile) signals the market is not pricing any of these risks — complacency is itself a risk factor.

The tension: Each risk is manageable in isolation; the danger is sequencing — a Brent spike widens CAD, weakens INR, forces RBI to hold rates longer, compresses bank NIMs, and tightens NBFC funding simultaneously.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a sustained print above $105/bbl triggers the CAD-INR-inflation feedback loop that the RBI's current pause cannot accommodate.

"}
